chapter: The 1920s road: dance style and management
title: What kind of man Nazarro was; the 1926 second injunction at the Sunset
summary: He calls Nazarro a Russian Jew with a heart of gold and the mind of Hitler, whose letter to Joe Glaser at the Sunset brought a second injunction.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Well, was he managing other groups, other than yourself initially?
When you first went with him.
You were the first act for him to manage you?
That's right. He just had this boy work with him as an understander.
What sort of guy was he?
Nazarro. How would you describe him?
Russian Jew, he was a Russian Jew. That was him. But he

appears to have a heart of gold, but a mind of Hitler. Do you understand what I'm saying? He wouldn't let up off on nothing. He wouldn't let up off on nothing. So I can only say that's all I can say about him, and God rest his soul he'll pay for his. He's dead and gone now. So my point now is that in going into the cabaret in Chicago, it was the year of 1926 that we were in Sunset because 1926 in the Sunset that's when we had the second injunction, that second letter from Nazarro going to the manager, which was Joe Glaser, telling him about us, that we were under contract to him.
